pharm: Synthetic anthracenedione that intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II, producing cytotoxic strand breaks; also immunomodulatory in multiple sclerosis.
quick: ~12 mg/m2 IV (AML 12 mg/m2 days 1-3; prostate 12-14 mg/m2 q21d; MS 12 mg/m2 q3 months)
Contraindicated (Category D); can cause fetal harm
Minor renal excretion; no specific scheme
Caution; MS patients with hepatic impairment should not be treated
LVEF (echo/MUGA), CBC, LFTs, cumulative dose; pregnancy test (MS)
summary: Mitoxantrone is an anthracenedione cytotoxic used for acute nonlymphocytic (myeloid) leukemia, advanced hormone-refractory prostate cancer (with corticosteroids), and worsening/progressive forms of multiple sclerosis. It carries boxed warnings for cardiotoxicity (potentially fatal heart failure, cumulative-dose related) and secondary acute myeloid leukemia. LVEF must be assessed before the initial dose and before each subsequent dose in MS, and a lifetime cumulative dose of 140 mg/m2 must not be exceeded in MS. It harmlessly turns urine and sometimes the sclera blue-green.
indications: Initial therapy of acute nonlymphocytic (myeloid) leukemia in adults, in combination with other agents
Pain of advanced hormone-refractory prostate cancer, in combination with corticosteroids
Secondary (chronic) progressive, progressive-relapsing, or worsening relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (not primary progressive MS)

dosage.t: With cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day continuous infusion days 1-7
dosage.n: Second induction (2 days mitoxantrone + 5 days cytarabine) if needed

dosage.t: With cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day continuous infusion days 1-5

dosage.n: Given with corticosteroids (e.g., prednisone 5 mg PO twice daily)
Lifetime cumulative dose must not exceed 140 mg/m2; assess LVEF before each dose

admin: Dilute to at least 50 mL with 0.9% sodium chloride or 5% dextrose
Infuse slowly into a freely running IV over not less than 3 minutes (AML/prostate); MS over ~5-15 minutes
Never give subcutaneously, intramuscularly, intra-arterially, or intrathecally (severe permanent injury)
For extravasation: stop immediately, restart in another vein, apply intermittent ice, and elevate the limb
Do not mix with heparin in the same infusion (precipitate forms); handle as a hazardous cytotoxic drug
moa: Mitoxantrone intercalates into DNA causing cross-links and strand breaks and inhibits topoisomerase II; it is cytocidal to both proliferating and non-proliferating cells (not cell-cycle-phase specific). In MS it suppresses B-cell, T-cell, and macrophage activity and proliferation.

absolute: MS patients with baseline LVEF below the lower limit of normal
MS cumulative dose already at or above 140 mg/m2
relative: Pre-existing cardiac disease or prior anthracycline/anthracenedione exposure
MS patients with hepatic impairment (should ordinarily not be treated)
monitor: Left ventricular ejection fraction (echo or MUGA)

preg: Pregnancy Category D - can cause fetal harm; avoid pregnancy during therapy. MS patients capable of becoming pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test confirmed before each dose.
lact: Mitoxantrone is excreted in human milk (detected up to 28 days after a dose); discontinue breastfeeding before starting therapy.
renal: Predominantly eliminated by biliary/fecal routes with only minor renal excretion; no specific renal dose adjustment is provided in the label.
hepatic: Clearance is reduced and exposure increased in hepatic impairment; no laboratory-based dosing scheme is given, and MS patients with hepatic impairment should ordinarily not be treated.

major: Other cardiotoxic agents (anthracyclines) - additive cumulative cardiotoxicity
Other myelosuppressive agents or radiotherapy - additive marrow suppression
minor: No significant interactions revealed in post-marketing cancer experience
interactions.diagnostics: Do not mix with heparin in the same line (precipitate); blue-green urine discoloration is expected after dosing.

common: Harmless blue-green urine and bluish sclera
serious: Cardiotoxicity / congestive heart failure and reduced LVEF (may be delayed months to years)

monitoring: LVEF by echocardiogram or MUGA before the initial dose and before every subsequent dose (MS); at cumulative thresholds in cancer
Complete blood count with platelets before each course
Liver function tests before each course
Serum uric acid in leukemia (start hypouricemic therapy before antileukemic treatment)
Pregnancy test before each dose in MS patients capable of becoming pregnant
Cumulative lifetime dose (cap 140 mg/m2 in MS)
counsel: Your urine may turn blue-green and the whites of your eyes may look bluish for about 24-48 hours - this is harmless
Use effective contraception and avoid pregnancy; report any possible pregnancy at once
Report symptoms of heart failure such as breathlessness, ankle swelling, or rapid weight gain
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bleeding, or bruising promptly (low blood counts)
Hair loss is common and usually reversible after treatment ends
pk: Cytotoxic effect over days; clinical response over treatment cycles
Terminal ~23-215 h (median ~75 h, i.e. days); distribution alpha 6-12 min, beta 1.1-3.1 h
Prolonged tissue retention; dosed on multi-week/monthly cycles
20-25 C; do not freeze; after vial entry use within 7 days at 15-25 C or 14 days refrigerated
pearls: Boxed warnings: potentially fatal cardiotoxicity (cumulative dose related) and secondary acute myeloid leukemia
In MS, the lifetime cumulative dose must never exceed 140 mg/m2 - track it meticulously
Assess LVEF before the first dose and before every subsequent dose in MS patients
Both heart failure and secondary leukemia can be delayed months to years, so monitoring continues after therapy ends
Pre-warn patients about harmless blue-green urine and bluish sclera
An anthracenedione, not an anthracycline, but shares anthracycline-like cardiotoxicity
missed: Given on a fixed schedule under specialist supervision; there is no patient self-administered make-up dose. Missed or delayed cycles are rescheduled by the treating oncology/neurology team with re-assessment of counts and LVEF.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Manage supportively with hematologic support (transfusions, growth factors) and antimicrobials for severe myelosuppression. Monitor cardiac and hepatic function closely. Mitoxantrone is not appreciably removed by dialysis.
